title: Simplicial mapping calculus with a fixed set of objects
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and the fixed-object model category $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus], and simplicial model categories and simplicial mapping spaces of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Use the Kan-model simplicial sets of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $O$ be any small set, including the empty set. For $B\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$ and a small simplicial set $K$, let $B^K$ have objects $O$, mapping sets $\operatorname{Fun}(K,B(u,v))$, pointwise composition using the diagonal of $K$, and constant identity maps. There are tensors adjoint to these cotensors. With
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(C,B)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}_O}(C,B^{\Delta^n}),$$
composition and simplicial operators given by pointwise composition and restriction, the fixed-object model structure is a simplicial model category. In particular, for a cofibration $C\to D$ and a local Kan fibration $B\to B'$, the corner map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(D,B)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(C,B)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(C,B')}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(D,B')$$
is a Kan fibration, trivial if either input map is also a local weak equivalence. For $u,v\in O$, the pair $u=v$ allowed, let $F_{uv}(K)=F^O_{u,v}(K)$ be the free simplicial category with objects $O$ on the simplicial family $K$ of generating arrows from $u$ to $v$, with its ordinary adjunction to evaluation at $(u,v)$, of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. This adjunction enriches to a simplicial Quillen adjunction $F_{uv}:\mathrm{sSet}_{\mathrm{Kan}}\rightleftarrows\mathrm{sCat}_O:\operatorname{ev}_{uv}$, with natural isomorphism
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_O(F_{uv}(K),B)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K,B(u,v)).$$

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Section 7.1 and Proposition 7.2, printed pp.276-277 (PDF pp.9-10 zero indexed), explicitly the closed simplicial model structure on SO-Cat; the displayed cotensor and free-generator adjunction spell out its obvious simplicial structure. No Stacks tag states this theorem. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix the small set O. The cited fixed-object free-calculus node supplies the category sCat_O and its model structure with local weak equivalences and local Kan fibrations, with functorial factorizations. By the sorted-theory identification, sCat_O is equivalent to the category of strict simplicial T_O-algebras for the O×O-sorted theory T_O, with evaluation at the sort ((u,v)) naturally isomorphic to the mapping set A↦A(u,v); this holds for u=v and for O=∅. The sorted-algebra model node therefore gives a model structure on sCat_O whose weak equivalences and fibrations are those detected by every evaluation A↦A(u,v), i.e. exactly the local weak equivalences and local Kan fibrations. A model structure is determined by its weak equivalences and fibrations (cofibrations are the maps with the left lifting property against trivial fibrations), so it is the fixed-object model structure. Its generating cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are F_s(∂Δ^m)→F_s(Δ^m) and F_s(Λ_i^m)→F_s(Δ^m) for the left adjoint F_s of evaluation at s=(u,v). The free-arrow adjunction exhibits F^O_{u,v} as a left adjoint of the same evaluation functor, so F_s≅F^O_{u,v} naturally, and the generating cells are the free-arrow maps F^O_{u,v}(∂Δ^m)→F^O_{u,v}(Δ^m) and F^O_{u,v}(Λ_i^m)→F^O_{u,v}(Δ^m), including u=v; for O=∅ the generating families are empty.

For B∈sCat_O and a small simplicial set K, set (B^K)(u,v)=Fun(K,B(u,v)); define composition by the diagonal K→K×K followed by the two mapping maps and B-composition, and let the identities be the constant maps at id_u. Associativity and units hold pointwise, so this is a simplicial category with object set O, functorial in K (contravariantly) and B. Limits in sCat_O are computed on mapping sets (the forgetful functors to the mapping sets are the sorted evaluations, which create limits of finite-product-preserving functors), and K↦Fun(K,B(u,v)) turns colimits of simplicial sets into limits; hence K↦B^K turns colimits into limits, and (B^K)^L≅B^{K×L} by currying, compatibly with the diagonal compositions. Define the tensor explicitly: (K⊗C)_n is the coproduct in ordinary categories with object set O (free product amalgamating identities) of copies C_n^{(k)} of C_n, one for each k∈K_n, and a simplicial operator α sends the copy indexed by k to the copy indexed by α^*k by α^* on arrows. A map K⊗C→B is, degreewise, a functor C_n→B_n for every k∈K_n, compatible with simplicial operators; equivalently, for all u,v a simplicial map K×C(u,v)→B(u,v) which for fixed k preserves composition and identities; by currying, a map of simplicial sets C(u,v)→Fun(K,B(u,v)) preserving the diagonal composition and constant identities, i.e. a map C→B^K. This gives Hom(K⊗C,B)≅Hom(C,B^K), naturally in K,C,B. The empty O case: sCat_∅ has one object and every construction is that object.

source.place: Section 7.1, displayed cotensor and tensor construction, printed p.276.

proof.text: Define Map_O(C,B)_n=Hom_sCat_O(C,B^{Δ^n}). A simplicial operator α:[m]→[n] acts by restriction along Δ^m→Δ^n. Since K↦B^K turns colimits into limits (step 2) and K is the colimit of its simplices, Hom_sSet(K,Map_O(C,B))≅Hom(C,B^K) naturally. Given maps C→D^{Δ^n} and D→B^{Δ^n}, apply (−)^{Δ^n} to the second, use (B^{Δ^n})^{Δ^n}=B^{Δ^n×Δ^n} and the diagonal Δ^n→Δ^n×Δ^n to obtain C→B^{Δ^n}; the identity is the constant identity functor. Associativity and the simplicial identities reduce to associativity, units and functoriality of restriction, and vertices of Map_O(C,B) are the maps C→B. Using (B^K)^{Δ^n}≅B^{K×Δ^n} and the natural bijection just proved, Map_O(C,B^K)_n=Hom(C,B^{K×Δ^n})≅Hom(K×Δ^n,Map_O(C,B))=[K,Map_O(C,B)]_n, and with step 2, Map_O(K⊗C,B)_n=Hom(K⊗C,B^{Δ^n})≅Hom(C,B^{K×Δ^n})≅[K,Map_O(C,B)]_n, compatibly with simplicial operators. These are the enriched tensor and cotensor isomorphisms of the simplicial tensor-cotensor definition, with universal elements given by the identities of K⊗C and B^K.

For a free generating cell F^O_{u,v}(i), with i a boundary or horn inclusion, and a simplicial monomorphism j, the new free-cell node, whose tensor is the one of step 2, identifies the tensor pushout product with F^O_{u,v}(i□j) and states that it is a cofibration, trivial if i is a horn inclusion or j is a weak homotopy equivalence. (Its hypotheses are exactly these; the trivial cases come from the anodyne pushout-product node, applied to i□j or, by the symmetry of the product, j□i, and anodyne maps are the trivial Kan cofibrations; F^O_{u,v} preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations since its right adjoint, evaluation at (u,v), preserves local Kan fibrations and trivial fibrations.) Hence every generating cofibration tensored with a simplicial monomorphism is a cofibration, trivial when the simplicial map is weak, and every generating trivial cofibration gives a trivial cofibration.

Apply the generator-extension lemma for the simplicial model axiom to the enrichment, tensors and cotensors of steps 2-3, with S the free boundary cells and T the free horn cells of step 1. By the free-arrow adjunction a map has the right lifting property against S (resp. T) exactly when each evaluation at (u,v) has it against all boundary (resp. horn) inclusions, i.e. is a trivial Kan fibration (resp. a Kan fibration) by the Kan node; so S^□=F∩W (trivial fibrations) and T^□=F (fibrations), as the sorted-algebra model node also states. The previous step verifies its pushout-product hypotheses for every monomorphism. It follows that the tensor-cotensor enrichment satisfies the simplicial model axiom: for every cofibration C→D and local Kan fibration B→B′, the corner map Map_O(D,B)→Map_O(C,B)×_{Map_O(C,B′)}Map_O(D,B′) is a Kan fibration, trivial if either input is a local weak equivalence. This is exactly the simplicial model-category assertion in the item.

For u,v∈O, the free-arrow adjunction gives Hom_sCat_O(F^O_{u,v}(K),B^{Δ^n})≅Hom_sSet(K,Fun(Δ^n,B(u,v))). By the cartesian closed adjunction for simplicial sets this is Fun(K,B(u,v))_n, naturally in n, K and B. These degreewise identifications commute with restriction and composition because both sides evaluate a functor on the length-one generators. Thus Map_O(F^O_{u,v}(K),B)≅Fun(K,B(u,v)). The free-arrow functor sends boundary and horn generating cofibrations to the corresponding fixed-object generating cells, so it is left Quillen; evaluation at (u,v), being objectwise on mapping sets, preserves local fibrations and trivial fibrations. This proves the simplicial Quillen adjunction and the asserted natural isomorphism, including loops and the empty-object case.

lean.statement: theorem fixed_object_simplicial_mapping_calculus (O : Type u) : ∃ s : SimplicialCategory (Fixed O), (∃ T : @SimplicialTensorCotensor (Fixed O) (fixedCategory O) s, (∀ (K : SSet.{u}) (B : Fixed O), T.cotensor K B = mappingCotensor K B)) ∧ @FixedMappingFormulas O s ∧ (∃ m : ModelCategory (Fixed O), m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = fixedWeakEquivalences O ∧ m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations = fixedFibrations O ∧ m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations = fixedCofibrations O ∧ @CategoryTheory.SimplicialModelLocalization.SatisfiesSM7 (Fixed O) (fixedCategory O) m s) ∧ (∀ (a b : O) (K L : SSet.{u}) (i : K ⟶ L), Mono i → fixedCofibrations O (freeArrowMap a b i) ∧ (Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence i → fixedWeakEquivalences O (freeArrowMap a b i)))
